name: Knight of the Round
body:
Followers of old ideals, wielders of swords, spears and shields, and armed to the teeth, the knights of the round serve ancient spirits of warriors and kings, and embody their style and code of honor.

Alignment: Any lawful

Hit Die: d10

Parent Classes: fighter, vigilante and medium

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175 gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Skills

Class Skills: The class skills of the knight of the round (and the key ability for each skill) are Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Points Per Level: 4 + Intelligence Modifier

Table: Knight of the Round
Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Features
1st	+1	+2	+0	+2	Embodiment, first step
2nd	+2	+3	+0	+3	Chivalric presence, chivalric talent, defensive training
3rd	+3	+3	+1	+3	Armor training 1
4th	+4	+4	+1	+4	Chivalric talent, second step
5th	+5	+4	+1	+4	Bonus feat
6th	+6/+1	+5	+2	+5	Chivalric talent
7th	+7/+2	+5	+2	+5	Armor training 2, third step
8th	+8/+3	+6	+2	+6	Chivalric talent
9th	+9/+4	+6	+3	+6	Bonus feat
10th	+10/+5	+7	+3	+7	Chivalric talent, fourth step
11th	+11/+6/+1	+7	+3	+7	Armor training 3
12th	+12/+7/+2	+8	+4	+8	Chivalric talent, fifth step
13th	+13/+8/+3	+8	+4	+8	Bonus feat
14th	+14/+9/+4	+9	+4	+9	Chivalric talent
15th	+15/+10/+5	+9	+5	+9	Armor training 4, sixth step
16th	+16/+11/+6/+1	+10	+5	+10	Chivalric talent
17th	+17/+12/+7/+2	+10	+5	+10	Bonus feat
18th	+18/+13/+8/+3	+11	+6	+11	Chivalric talent, seventh step
19th	+19/+14/+9/+4	+11	+6	+11	Armor training 5
20th	+20/+15/+10/+5	+12	+6	+12	Chivalric talent, final embodiment
Class Features
Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

All knights of the round are proficient with all simple and martial weapons, as well as light, medium and heavy armor and shields, although this might be modified by embodiment.

Embodiment

The knights of the round all seek to embody one of the legendary knights of the round table, and master their unique fighting style and techniques.

At 1st level, the knight of the round chooses a spirit for their embodiment feature. This determines what each of the steps do at later levels, and modifies the knight of the round’s proficiencies. The spirits are listed clearly on page 8. Once a spirit is chosen, it cannot be changed.

Each step is an ability granted by the spirit chosen by the knight of the round. You gain your first step at 1st level, then every three levels thereafter and a final, full embodiment at 20th level.

Chivalric Presence (Ex)

Knights of the round are combatants of high nobility, and as such, also capable of holding themselves on the social battleground as well as the physical one.

At 2nd level, the knight of the round gets a social outfit designed to display their nobility or other high standing, and allow them to mingle with high society. The outfit counts as clothing, and provides a +1 morale bonus to Diplomacy, which increases by +1 at 6th, 12th and 18th levels. This bonus does not function outside of high society settings such as a noble’s home or a ball. This is subject to GM discretion.

In addition, chivalric presence grants the knight of the round a social identity, one that is separate from their knightly legends they intend to create. While unarmored and wearing their chivalry outfit, the knight of the round is assumed to be using their social identity.

Chivalric Talents

At 2nd level, and every even level afterwards, the knight of the round can choose a chivalric talent for which they meet the prerequisites.

Chivalric talents function as long as the knight of the round is unarmored and wearing their chivalry outfit.

Chivalric talents are listed on page 3.

Defensive Training (Ex)

Starting at 2nd level, a knight of the round counts their total knight of the round level as his fighter level for the purpose of qualifying for any armor or shield-related feats. If they have levels in fighter, these levels stack.

Armor Training (Ex)

Starting at 3rd level, a knight of the round learns to be more maneuverable while wearing armor. Whenever they are wearing armor, they reduces the armor check penalty by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by their armor by 1. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, 15th and 19th), these bonuses increase by +1 each time, to a maximum –5 reduction of the armor check penalty and a +5 increase of the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed. In addition, a knight of the round can also move at their normal speed while wearing medium armor.

At 7th level, a knight of the round can move at their normal speed while wearing heavy armor. If the knight of the round has levels in another class that gains armor training, the class levels stack together with other classes to determine the bonuses and ability to gain advanced armor training.

Bonus Feat

At 5th level and every 4 levels afterwards, the knight of the round can pick a bonus combat feat for which they meet the prerequisites.

Full Embodiment

At 20th level, the knight of the round fully embodies the spirit they have chosen. As long as they are under the effect of any of their abilities, or have used one in the last minute, the knight of the round gains DR 10/- and a +2 luck bonus to all stats.

This does not stack with itself, but triggering this ability within the duration resets it.

Chivalric Talents
Always Prepared (Ex)

The knight of the round can set aside resources to plan for future contingencies. The knight of the round gains the Brilliant Planner feat except they can spend up to 100 gp per character level for their brilliant plan fund and only requires 1 minute to enact their brilliant plan. In addition, while in a settlement for at least 1 week, they can spend 24 hours and up to 500 gp per character level to create a stash somewhere within the settlement. Once per day, the knight of the round can take 1 hour to retrieve a stash, retrieving any number of items that would have been available in a settlement they visited at the time of making the stash, regardless of the weight of the items.

Once they retrieve a stash in this way, they subtract the price of the items from the stash’s value and the stash is exhausted and lost, regardless if they use the full value of the stash. The knight of the round can maintain any number of stashes, but a stash is lost if they do not spend 1 hour to maintain the stash at least once per month. A knight of the round’s stash is well-hidden and only the knight of the round knows the location of a stash they create.

Ancestral Enlightenment (Ex)

The knight of the round can attempt any Knowledge check untrained. If they already have ranks in a particular Knowledge skill, he gains a +4 bonus on checks with that skill. A knight of the round must be at least 5th level to select this talent.

Any Guise (Su)

A knight of the round can use his everyman social talent to disguise themselves as any specific person, even a king or high priest. Furthermore, if the actual individual wouldn’t normally be able to be found via magic (such as by being dead or protected from divinations designed to locate the individual), such divinations always find the knight of the round instead. A knight of the round must be at least 17th level and have the everyman social talent to select this talent.

Beast Friend (Su)

The knight of the round can cast charm animal once per day as a spell-like ability, with a caster level equal to their level. The knight of the round must have the songbird social talent to select this talent.

Beast Speech (Su)

The knight of the round can cast speak with animals once per day as a spell-like ability, with a caster level equal to their character level. The knight of the round must have the songbird social talent to select this talent.

Case the Joint (Ex)

The knight of the round can use their social identity to learn important facts about a location before returning later in his knight of the round identity. If they spend at least 1 hour in a location while in their social identity, they can attempt a DC 20 Knowledge (engineering) check. If they succeed, they gain the ability to later reroll any one failed skill check involving the location’s layout (such as a Stealth check to sneak into the location, a Disable Device check to disable an alarm, or a Sleight of Hand check to snatch an object from a pedestal). For every 10 by which the check exceeds 20, the knight of the round gains an additional reroll. If the knight of the round fails to return to the location within 1 week, the situation changes too much and they cannot use the rerolls. A knight of the round can’t case the same joint more than once a week.

Celebrity Discount (Ex)

The knight of the round’s social identity is popular enough to receive discounts in their area of renown. Whenever they buy an item in their area of renown that costs 500 gp or less, they can buy it at 90% of the market price, rather than the full price. If they have the great renown social talent, the gp limit increases to 2,000 gp, and if he possesses the incredible renown social talent, the gp limit increases to 8,000 gp. A knight of the round must be at least 3rd level and have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Celebrity Perks (Ex)

The knight of the round is a celebrity in their area of renown, and adoring fans are all too eager to shower them with the fundamental necessities. While within their area of renown, they can always receive common meals or lodging (worth up to 1 gp per meal or night) for free, and can avoid paying taxes or bribes of 1 gp or less. If they want a particular non-magical item worth 1 gp or less, they can spend 1d10 minutes interacting with people in their area of renown to receive the item from a fan (if they ever sells such a gift from a fan, they lose this social talent permanently). If they have the great renown social talent, they can receive gifts of up to 5 gp, receive fine food and lodgings (worth up to 10 gp per meal or night) for free, and avoid paying taxes or bribes of 10 gp or less. If they have incredible renown, they can receive gifts of up to 25 gp, receive exquisite food and lodgings (worth up to 100 gp per meal or night) for free, and avoid paying taxes or bribes of 100 gp or less. A knight of the round must be at least 5th level and have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Double Time (Ex)

The knight of the round’s social identity is that of a skilled and respected artisan or professional, rather than a merchant or noble. In order to complete their day’s work while still continuing their knight of the round activities, they have learned to work faster than normal, hiding their progress so it seems like they are working full shifts at their day job rather than spending some of that time on other pursuits. The knight of the round needs to spend only 6 hours each day for mundane uses of the Artistry, Craft or Profession skill, rather than 8 hours. If they have the social grace social talent, they need to spend only 4 hours for any skill they’ve chosen with social grace. A knight of the round must have a social identity appropriate to the chosen skill to select this talent.

Entrepreneur (Ex)

Select any one Intelligence-, Wisdom-, or Charisma-based skill other than Perception or Use Magic Device. The knight of the round can use the selected skill to earn money as if they were using a Profession skill. If they select Artistry, Perform or Profession, the knight of the round instead gains the skill unlock powers for those skills as appropriate for their number of ranks in that skill. If they have the social grace social talent, they can apply this benefit to all skills selected with the social grace talent.

Everyman (Su)

The knight of the round can take on the appearance of a specific individual whenever they assume a mundane guise using their many guises social talent. The individual must be a farmer, laborer, or peasant. While disguised as this individual, the knight of the round receives a +20 circumstance bonus on Disguise checks to appear as that individual. Any spell or ability designed to locate the individual has a 50% chance of finding the knight of the round instead of the actual individual, and divination spells and abilities used on the knight of the round give results as if they were the actual individual. Although this doesn’t grant the knight of the round any special knowledge of the individual, the knight of the round’s training grants them a +10 circumstance bonus on Bluff checks to properly play the part of the individual. A knight of the round must be at least 11th level and have the many guises social talent to select this talent.

Feign Innocence (Ex)

The knight of the round’s social identity seems so innocent that it is hard to believe they were involved in wrongdoing. Within their area of renown, this provides a non-magical effect identical to the innocence spell. A knight of the round must be at least 5th level and have the renown social talent to take this talent.

Gossip Collector (Ex)

The knight of the round sits at the center of a web of gossip, granting them access to the latest scuttlebutt with baffling speed. Whenever the knight of the round is presented with a topic about which they would normally need to spend 1d4 hours to gather information, they must spend only 1d2 hours instead. If they have the renown social talent and gathers the information in their area of renown, they must instead spend only 1d4 × 10 minutes, and if they beat the DC to gather a piece of information by 20 or more, they know that piece of information without spending any time at all; they have simply already heard that gossip. This ability doesn’t allow them to gather information that isn’t available in the locale they are canvassing, even if that locale is his area of renown. The knight of the round must have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Great Renown (Ex)

The knight of the round is known on a broader scale. They can gain renown in a single community of up to 5,000 individuals (a large town) or up to two communities of no more than 2,000 individuals each (two small towns). The bonus while they are in their social identity remains unchanged, but the circumstance bonus on Intimidate checks from their renown social talent while they are in their knight of the round identity increases to +6. A knight of the round must be at least 7th level and have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Guise of Life (Su)

An undead knight of the round with this talent gains an additional social identity in the form of one living creature identical to the knight of the round’s appearance in life. Successful Knowledge checks reveal information about the knight of the round as if they were a living creature, and they count as living for the purpose of divination spells and effects. They gain no other benefit from appearing to be a living creature, and remains vulnerable to positive energy and spells that affect undead. The knight of the round must be a corporeal undead creature to select this talent. Humanoid knights of the round with the negative energy affinity racial trait can also select this talent, gaining a human social identity

Guise of Unlife (Su)

A knight of the round with this talent gains an additional social identity in the form of an undead version of one of their existing social identities, such as a ghoul, vampire, or zombie. Successful Knowledge checks reveal information about the knight of the round as if they were undead, and they counts as undead for the purpose of divination spells and effects. They gain no other benefit from appearing to be an undead creature, and remains vulnerable to negative energy and spells that effect the living. The knight of the round must be a living creature to select this talent.

Immediate Change (Ex)

The knight of the round can change identities as a move action, and they no longer need to spend extra time to adjust their appearance and persona. A knight of the round must be at least 13th level and must have the quick change social talent to select this talent.

In Vogue (Ex)

The knight of the round’s crafting or professional business is always at the height of the local trends, allowing the knight of the round to gain more profits than usual. Goods or works they craft with an Artistry or Craft skill they chose with social grace are worth 1/3 more gp than normal due to their celebrity, without increasing the cost to create. Whenever they use an Artistry or Profession skill they chose with social grace to make money, they make twice as much money. A knight of the round must be at least 5th level and have both the double time and social grace social talents to take this talent.

Incredible Renown (Ex)

The knight of the round is incredibly famous in both identities. They can gain renown in a single community of up to 25,000 individuals (a large city) or up to two smaller cities of no more than 10,000 individuals each (two small cities). The bonus while they are in their social identity remains unchanged, but the circumstance bonus to Intimidate from their great renown social talent while in they are in their knight of the round identity increases to +8. A knight of the round must be at least 11th level and have the great renown social talent to select this talent.

Instant Recognition (Ex)

The knight of the round is so well known that his name precedes him, even to other communities. It only takes 4 hours of effort to get the word out to transfer their renown benefits to a new community. A knight of the round must be at least 13th level and have both the incredible renown and triumphant return social talents to select this talent.

Intrigue Feats (Ex)

The knight of the round gains one of the following feats as a bonus feat: Blustering Bluff, But a Scratch, Call Truce, Confabulist, Criminal Reputation, Cutting Humiliation, Esoteric Linguistics, Intoxicating Flattery, Ironclad Logic, Nerve-Racking Negotiator, Orator, Persuasive Bribery, Play to the Crowd, Quick Favor, Rhetorical Flourish, Sense Assumptions, Sense Relationships, or Street Smarts. They must meet the feat’s prerequisites. This talent can be selected multiple times; each time, the knight of the round gains a new feat from the above list.

Loyal Aid (Ex)

The knight of the round gains the service of a number of loyal allies who can help them gather information, cover for their two identities, or perform minor tasks. Inside their area of renown, a knight of the round with this talent gains a bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information equal to half their knight of the round level. In addition, if the knight of the round wants, they can task their friends to help cover for them by spreading false tales of their location and activities to others. This has the effect of increasing the DC of Diplomacy checks to gather information about the knight of the round and Survival checks to track them by an amount equal to their level. This lasts for 1 day, and can be used only once per week. Finally, once per day, the knight of the round can ask their allies to perform a minor task for them. This usually involves delivering a message, purchasing a piece of mundane gear worth 100 gp or less (which the knight of the round must pay for), or retrieving an object owned by the knight of the round (that would be easily accessible by the ally). This task might take other forms as well, subject to GM discretion, but can never involve combat or danger. A knight of the round must be at least 3rd level and have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Many Guises (Ex)

The knight of the round can take on any number of mundane guises. Whenever they change their identity, they have a third option (instead of social or knight of the round): they can become mundane. The mundane identity is not a specific individual. Each one is created at the moment it is assumed, and quickly forgotten as soon as it is removed. While in a mundane identity, the knight of the round does not gain the benefit of either their social or knight of the round identity, but instead appears as a member of their ancestry, usually a common laborer, farmer, or peasant of any gender. Their alignment is treated as neutral when they are in their mundane identity. While in this identity, they receive a +20 circumstance bonus on Disguise checks to appear like an ordinary member of their ancestry. Spells and abilities that are looking for the knight of the round in either of their other identities fail while they are in their mundane identity. They must build the appearance for this identity using whatever clothing and tools they have at their disposal. While they can use magic (such as a hat of disguise), their mundane identity can never be anything other than an ordinary member of a society or large group (subject to GM discretion). A knight of the round must be at least 5th level to select this talent.

Mockingbird (Ex)

A Knight of the round must be at least 5th level to choose this talent.

The knight of the round can mimic almost any sort of voice, or even animal calls and sound effects, and he can throw his voice at a distance. This functions similarly to a combination of the ghost sound, ventriloquism, and vocal alteration spells.

Morphic Mask (Su)

The knight of the round’s physical form in their knight of the round identity can differ significantly from that of their social identity, within the norms for their ancestry—this can include changes to the knight of the round’s proportions, coloration, gender characteristics, and other physical characteristics. This increases the knight of the round’s bonus from seamless guise by 2 for every significant change, as per the Disguise skill. The knight of the round always assumes the same form when using this ability. A knight of the round with multiple natural forms, such as a kitsune, can alter each of their forms using this talent.

Owl’s Sight (Ex)

The knight of the round gains low-light vision. If they already have low-light vision, they gain a +4 competence bonus on Perception checks in dim light. The knight of the round also gains a +2 competence bonus on Sleight of Hand and Stealth checks at night.

Quick Change (Ex)

The knight of the round learns to shift between their identities with ease. Instead of needing 1 minute to change their identity, they can now do so as a full-round action. If, after a quick change, they encounters any creature familiar with both of their identities, they must attempt a Disguise check to avoid the creature seeing through their hastily donned disguise and realizing that the identities are, in fact, the same person. The knight of the round can spend 1 additional round adjusting and perfecting their appearance and persona to negate the need for this check. A knight of the round must be at least 7th level to select this talent.

Renown (Ex)

The knight of the round becomes known for deeds and abilities regardless of their current identity. This renown grants them favorable treatment in civilized company and lends them an air of menace while facing down their enemies. While they are in their social identity, a knight of the round can spend 1 week gaining renown among the locals of any community of no more than about 200 individuals (a village, if using settlement population ranges). This could be the entire community or a smaller neighborhood in a larger settlement. They must spend at least 4 hours each day socializing and making contacts. After spending 1 week doing this, whenever they are in their social identity, all NPCs in the community have a starting attitude toward them that is one category better, as long as each person’s initial attitude would have at least been indifferent (see the Diplomacy skill description). While they gain renown in an area using their social identity, they also spread rumors and tales about their knight of the round identity. Once they have gained renown in a community, they gain a +4 circumstance bonus on Intimidate checks whenever they are in their knight of the round identity. This bonus applies only while they are near the community in which they have gained renown; they must be within a number of miles equal to their knight of the round level. A knight of the round can hold renown in a limited number of communities (normally one, with other social talents allowing two). If they gain renown in a new community, they must decide which one of their previous communities to lose. These effects are subject to GM approval. For example, the GM might rule that an Npc or monster has not heard any tales about the knight of the round. Or, a foe may have a starting attitude toward him that’s one category worse, rather than one category better.

Safe House (Ex)

The knight of the round can establish a safe house in their area of renown, and they can change it every time they change their area of renown. If they don’t have the renown talent, they can still select this talent and place the safe house in a single location to which they have access, but they can never move the safe house from its initial location until they gain the renown talent. This safe house must be an area no larger in volume than a cube that is a number of feet per side equal to 10 feet per class level. The safe house can be arranged any way they like and it can be part of a larger building, like a secret room or an underground cave. Objects within this safe house can’t be located by any effect that is less powerful than a discern location spell.

At 7th level, this protection from being located also applies to creatures in the safe house.

At 13th level, the entire area is protected from scrying effects (though not mundane snooping) like a mage’s private sanctum.

Skill Familiarity (Ex)

The knight of the round chooses four skills when they gain this talent. They can take 10 on checks with their chosen skills even when distracted or threatened. If they take 10 on checks with these skills while not distracted or threatened, they gain a bonus on the check equal to one-quarter their class level (minimum +2). A knight of the round must be at least 9th level to select this talent.

Social Grace

The knight of the round selects any one Intelligence-, Wisdom-, or Charisma-based skill other than Perception or Use Magic Device. Whenever they are in their social identity, they receive a +4 circumstance bonus on checks with the selected skill.

At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, they can select another skill (with the same restrictions) to gain this bonus.

Songbird (Su)

The knight of the round gains the use of animal messenger once per day as a spell-like ability, with a caster level equal to their character level. They also gain Handle Animal as a class skill.

Subjective Truth (Ex)

The knight of the round’s disparate identities allow them to defeat magic that detects lies. As long as what they say is true from the point of view of their current identity, it detects as true to effects such as discern lies, and they can say it in effects such as zone of truth that force them to speak the truth. A knight of the round must be at least 9th level and have the feign innocence social talent to select this talent.

Triumphant Return (Ex)

The knight of the round’s tales are never truly forgotten. This makes it easier to establish their renown in a place they have established it before. In any settlement where the knight of the round previously gained renown, it takes only 3 days, rather than 1 week, to gain renown again. A knight of the round must be at least 3rd level and have the renown social talent to select this talent.

Well-Known Expert (Ex)

The knight of the round’s social identity is known as an expert in numerous fields, including areas and topics the knight of the round hasn’t actually taken the time to study. As a result they are skilled at encouraging others to discover solutions to difficult problems themselves by asking probing questions, while appearing to give the information themselves. In their social identity, the knight of the round can take 10 when attempting to aid another on Appraise, Artistry, Craft, and Knowledge checks. They also gain a bonus equal to half their class level (minimum +1) on Bluff checks to appear knowledgeable in Appraise, Artistry, Craft (all), and Knowledge (all). If they have the renown social talent, they grant a +3 bonus when they successfully aid another on these skill checks, rather than +2. In their area of renown, the knight of the round’s social identity is so trusted as an expert that scholars are inspired to make amazing deductions and intuitive leaps in discussions with them. A creature that has already failed a Knowledge check on a specific subject can attempt one additional check to gain information on the same topic if it receives an aid another bonus from the knight of the round when doing so.

Other Social Talents

The knight of the round can select other social talents available to the vigilante as long as they deal with Charisma-based skills, the arts or other noble pursuits.

Spirits
Arthur

Knights of the round who follow Arthur are born leaders, who lead from the front and inspire greatness for their allies.

First Step (Su)

At 1st level, a knight of the round that embodies the once and future king exudes an aura of calm and determination. All allies, including the knight of the round, within 10 feet gain a +2 morale bonus on saving throws against emotion effects. This aura only functions while the knight of the round is conscious, not if they are unconscious or dead.

Second Step (Su)

At 4th level, the knight of the round can bolster their allies with their commanding presence. For a number of rounds equal to their class level plus their Charisma modifier, the knight of the round can extend the radius of their aura from the first step and add the benefits of the bless spell to any allies within the radius as a free action. The rounds need not be consecutive. This is a mind-affecting, emotion effect.

Third Step (Su)

At 7th level, the knight of the round, the knight of the round can summon the fabled sword of their spirit to use against their foes. As a standard action the knight of the round may summon the sword which acts as a +1 adamantine bastard sword. The knight of the round gains proficiency with the sword if they do not already have proficiency with bastard swords. Every 3 levels after 7th the sword increases its enhancement bonus by 1 to a maximum of +5 at 19th level.

At 10th level, the sword gains the keen special weapon ability, at 15th it gains the glorious weapon special ability and at 20th it also gains the defiant weapon special ability. The knight of the round can summon the weapon for a number of minutes equal to their class level. The minutes need not be consecutive but must be used in 1-minute intervals. This sword cannot be picked up or given to another, if it leaves the knight of the round’s possession, it reappears in their hand instantly. Dismissing the sword is a swift action.

Fourth Step (Su)

At 10th level, when activating the extended aura from their second step, the knight of the round instead grants the benefits of prayer to their allies. In addition, enemies within the aura must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the knight of the round’s class level + their Charisma modifier) or suffer the penalties of the prayer spell effect while within the aura’s effect while this ability is active. This is a mind-affecting, emotion effect.

Fifth Step (Su)

At 12th level, the knight of the round can rally their allies. As a swift action, they can allow one ally within radius of their aura, extended or otherwise, to roll a saving throw against an ongoing effect that has, or had an initial, saving throw. Doing so costs 4 rounds of the empowered aura from the second step.

Sixth Step (Su)

Beginning at 15th level, they channel the power of the weapon of their spirit to form it into a powerful mount. Instead of summoning the weapon from the third step, the knight of the round can use the ability to summon a mount as a paladin equal to their class level. The knight of the round can have both simultaneously but it uses 3 minutes for every minute used by this ability.

Seventh Step (Su)

At 18th level, the knight of the round no longer need to expend minutes to have either the sword from the third step or the mount from the sixth step active, though having both active simultaneously uses 2 minutes per minute of duration used.

Galahad

Knights of the round who follow Galahad master the shield, focusing their skills into guarding allies, and protecting the meek.

First Step (Su)

At 1st level, the knight of the round learns to surround their allies in a field of holy protective energy. Whenever they make an attack roll on an enemy combatant, the knight of the round may apply a guardian’s shield to one ally (other than themselves) within 60 feet as a free action. This shield lasts for a number of rounds equal to the knight of the round’s Wisdom modifier. A guardian’s shield grants the affected ally a number of temporary hit points equal to twice the knight of the round’s class level. These temporary hit points do not stack with other temporary hit points, and vanish when the shield’s duration expires. The knight of the round can use their guardian’s shield ability a number of times per day equal to half their knight of the round class level (minimum 1) + their Wisdom modifier. This ability counts as the lay on hands class feature for the purposes of the Extra Lay on Hands feat.

Second Step (Ex)

At 4th level, the knight of the round gains Cry of Mercy as a bonus feat, without needing to meet its prerequisite. In addition, they can perform it more than once per day, spending a use of their first step ability to do so if it is the second time or more in a day. These uses can also affect enemies or allies within 30 feet of the knight of the round, chosen upon using the feat.

Third Step (Ex)

At 7th level, the knight of the round can, as an immediate action that uses an attack of opportunity, move up to half of their movement to intercept a charge targeting an ally within that distance. They must end between the charge initiator and his ally to be able to use this feature, but otherwise may stop the charge anywhere along the charger’s path as long as it is within the movement range. The movement is then taken out of their movement for the next turn. The charge attack is resolved against the knight of the round, as normal. If the target is intercepted within 10 feet of the charge’s origin, the charger does not gain the attack bonus, but still suffers the armor penalty.

Fourth Step (Su)

At 10th level, a knight of the round is trained in how best to control their enemies and their behavior in battle, urging attackers to throw their all against the knight of the round’s indomitable armor and unyielding shield. With a sharp blade, a clever taunt, or something that otherwise attracts her foe, the knight of the round can direct the attention of enemies towards themselves. Whenever the knight of the round attacks a foe in combat and inflicts at least 1 point of damage, as a free action they may mark the target as their foe and attempt to continue to force them to engage the knight of the round only. They may even mark a foe during an attack of opportunity and may make the free action to do so, even though it is not their turn. The target is aware of being marked, and the mark remains for a number of rounds equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). Marked targets suffer a -4 penalty to attack rolls against foes that are not the knight of the round, and arcane spellcasters suffer an increase in arcane spell failure of 10% + 1% per two class levels until the mark expires. The knight of the round may only maintain a number of marks equal to 3 + their Wisdom modifier, and they may make a number of marks per day equal to 1/2 their class level + their Wisdom modifier. This ability only functions on creatures with an Intelligence score of 1 or more, allowing them to mark animals and other beasts as well as sentient beings, but not mindless creatures such as skeletons. Multiple marks do not stack on the same target.

Fifth Step (Su)

At 12th level, the penalty imposed by the knight of the round’s fourth step ability is increased to -6. Additionally, the mark must make a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 knight of the round’s class level + their Wisdom modifier) to attempt attacking anyone other than the knight of the round. If a marked target succeeds the Will save, the mark is immediately removed. If the mark is removed in this manner, the target must make a second Will save at the same DC, or suffer the effects of Cry of Mercy for the rest of the original mark’s duration.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, the knight of the round can intercept area of effect attacks, as long as they have enough movement to get between the source and their ally. This is done as an immediate action, and the ally no longer has to make the save, but the knight of the round makes the save twice, taking the lower result in return for negating their ally’s injuries or maladies.

Seventh Step (Su)

At 18th level, the penalty imposed by the knight of the round’s fourth step ability is increased to -8, and now functions regardless of the target’s Intelligence. Any creature marked by the knight of the round, or attacking a target protected by guardian shield, suffers the effect of Cry of Mercy for that attack if the target is not the knight of the round itself.

Gawain

Knights of the round who follow Gawain focus on hefty two handed weapons, with huge blows to rain down and shatter through defenses.

First Step (Ex)

At 1st level, the knight of the round gains Improved Sunder as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. In addition, when using the sunder combat maneuver while wielding a weapon in two hands, any damage dealt to the target item over its current hp is transferred to the holder of the item, as if hit by an attack with that amount of damage.

Second Step (Ex)

At 4th level, the knight of the round can punch through defenses most consider impenetrable. They can ignore an amount of hardness of items equal to half their knight of the round level. This also applies to the natural hardness of constructs.

Third Step (Ex)

At 7th level, when the knight of the round successfully breaks an item with a sunder combat maneuver, they can make an attack on the holder of that item as a free action, using their highest base attack bonus. This attack cannot be a combat maneuver, and cannot be used if it was triggered from a sunder in a full attack, but can trigger from a successful sunder caused by the fourth step ability.

Fourth Step (Ex)

At 10th level, as a standard action, the knight of the round can make a single attack with a two handed weapon. If the attack hits, the knight of the round can make a sunder attempt as a free action on the same target that does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Fifth Step (Ex)

At 12th level, the knight of the round gains Greater Sunder as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. If they already have Greater Sunder, they may take a feat of their choice for which they meet the prerequisites. In addition, the bonuses from the second step feature increase to his full knight of the round class level.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, the knight of the round ignores DR equal to half of his knight of the round level when using a two handed weapon. In addition, if he successfully sunders the armor of a creature with DR, that DR is reduced by this amount for all attacks for a number of rounds equal to the armor bonus of the worn armor of the target.

Seventh Step (Ex)

At 18th level, the knight of the round gains double his strength bonus on the damage of two handed weapons, instead of the normal 1.5x increase. This bonus strength also applies to the damage of sunder attempts.

Lancelot

Knights of the round who follow Lancelot are masters of the spear, and focus purely on that route of combat.

They lose proficiency in shields, but gain proficiency in all weapons in the spears and polearm weapon groups.

First Step (Ex)

At 1st level, as an immediate action, a knight of the round can shorten the grip on their spear or polearm with reach and use it against adjacent targets. This action results in a –4 penalty on attack rolls with that weapon until they spend another immediate action to return to the normal grip. The penalty is reduced by –1 for every four levels beyond 1st. This ability can also be used to add reach to a nonreach polearm, with the same penalties and action requirements.

Second Step (Ex)

At 4th level, as a full attack action, a knight of the round can strike at a target within 5 feet of them, ignoring the penalty for their 1st level feature. If this strike hits, the knight of the round may then attack a target directly behind the first, resolving as a second separate hit, both at the knight of the round’s full base attack bonus. This can be used a number of times equal to 3 + the knight of the round’s Wisdom modifier. This ability can also be used to strike a target as if they had reach, and then hit a closer target while using a non-reach polearm.

Third Step (Ex)

At 7th level, a knight of the round may choose any square adjacent to them and treat that square as their occupied square for determining who they are flanking, even if that square is occupied by a creature, object, or solid barrier.

Fourth Step (Ex)

At 10th level, a knight of the round can use any spear or polearm to make bull rush maneuvers, though they take a –4 penalty on combat maneuver checks when making such attempts. When using a spear or polearm to make a trip maneuver, they treats these weapons as if they have the trip weapon feature.

Fifth Step (Ex)

At 12th level, when a creature threatened by a knight of the round takes a 5-foot step into or out of a square adjacent to them, the knight of the round can take a 5-foot step as an immediate action. This 5-foot step must be subtracted from their movement on the next turn. They also gain a +2 dodge bonus to their AC against that opponent until the end of their next turn.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, when an opponent threatened by a knight of the round makes a melee attack against an ally within reach of the knight of the round’s weapon, they may take an immediate action to grant their ally a +2 shield bonus to AC and DR 5/— against that attack. They may use this ability to protect themselves, but only if the attacking creature is not adjacent to them.

Seventh Step (Ex)

At 18th level, the knight of the round treats all polearm and spear weapons as reaching an additional 5 feet, regardless of using their 1st level feature or not. This stacks with the increasing reach of the 1st level feature, allowing a weapon to threaten at 5 and 10 feet, or 10 and 15 feet respectively.

Lucan

Knights of the round who follow Lucan dedicate themselves to guardianship and comradeship, aiding their liege lord and allies to their full capability.

First Step (Ex)

At 1st level, the knight of the round can select one of their allies to designate as their liege. Designating a liege takes a minute in which the knight bows to their lord and announces their dedication. The knight of the round may change their liege once per day. The knight of the round has a +2 bonus to making aid another checks for their liege and grant them a +1 bonus to AC when within reach or adjacent. Additionally, the knight can select Skill Focus or teamwork feats in place of their bonus combat feats.

Second Step (Ex)

At 4th level, the knight gains the ability to shield their allies from harm. As an immediate action when an adjacent or within reach ally is attacked you may jump in harm’s way to protect them. The ally gains +2 AC against the attack but if the attack misses by this bonus, the attacker makes a new attack roll (with the same modifier) targeting the knight of the round instead. Additionally, when an adjacent ally or an ally within reach makes a Reflex save, the knight of the round may throw themselves to help as well, as an immediate action. If the knight of the round was not already targeted by the effect, they must also make the Reflex save as if targeted by the effect and can take a penalty to their saving throw, up to their knight of the round level, granting their ally a bonus equal to the penalty taken. This feature is treated as Ally Shield for effects, and the knight is considered to have Ally Shield for prerequisites.

Third Step (Ex)

At 7th level, the knight’s ability to defend their allies improves. The knight may use a full-round action to enter a battle-trained support mode, allowing them to make two aid another checks with the same action. These aid another attempts may be both to the same ally or different allies and while using this step the knight of the round treats their reach as 5 feet farther for the purposes of making aid another checks and being in reach of allies for their knight of the round class features until the end of the next round.

At 12th and 17th levels, the knight of the round may make an additional aid another check as part of this ability.

Fourth Step (Ex)

At 10th level, the knight of the round learns to specialize in supporting their allies in all aspects both on and off the battlefield. The knight gains a +1 in all trained skills that aren’t class skills and can select a skill to specialize in, gaining Skill Focus in that skill, as well as treating that skill as a class skill if it was not already.

At 12th level, the bonus to trained skills that aren’t class skills raises to +2, and at 18th level, the Knight treats all skills as class skills.

Fifth Step (Ex)

At 12th level, the knight of the round increases their defense provided to their liege. The AC bonus granted to their liege increases by +1 and when making aid another checks for their liege, they increase the bonus given by +2. When using their second step ability to jump in the way of an attack for their liege, the knight of the round may choose to take half of the damage dealt even if the liege is still hit. This damage can not be reduced or negated in anyway.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, the knight is so committed to their liege that they will press on even with mortal injuries. As long as their designated liege is alive, the knight of the round is treated as if having the Diehard feat. While below 0 hit points and Diehard is active, the knight can only take movement, defensive actions, such as total defense, healing or any aid another actions. They may not take any actions that deal damage. If adjacent to their liege when they move, the knight of the round may move along with them for free, but must end their movement adjacent to their liege. If the knight already possess or gains the Diehard feat, they may use the feat as normal but no longer take any damage after taking an aid another action and if adjacent to their liege when they move, the knight may move along with them for free, but must end their movement adjacent to their liege.

Seventh Step (Ex)

At 18th level, the knight of the round has become a master of their craft, truly dedicating themselves to the round table. They may now designate an amount of lieges equal to 1 + their Charisma modifier.

Mordred

Knights of the round who follow Mordred disregard their honor and do anything to win, in social combat and the battlefield. Such knights of the round lose heavy armor proficiencies, and are not proficient in shields aside from the buckler.

First Step (Ex)

If a knight of the round can catch an opponent when they are unable to defend themselves effectively from the knight of the round’s attack, the knight of the round can strike a vital spot for extra damage. The knight of the round’s attack deals extra damage anytime their target would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC, whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not, or when the knight of the round flanks their target. This extra damage is 1d6 at 1st level, and increases by 1d6 every time they gain a new step ability. Ranged attacks can count as sneak attacks only if the target is within 30 feet. This additional damage is precision damage and is not multiplied on a critical hit. With a weapon that deals nonlethal damage, such as a sap, unarmed strike, or whip, a knight of the round can make a sneak attack that deals nonlethal damage instead of lethal damage. They cannot use a weapon that deals lethal damage to deal nonlethal damage in a sneak attack—not even with the usual –4 penalty. The knight of the round must be able to see the target well enough to pick out a vital spot and must be able to reach such a spot. A knight of the round cannot sneak attack while striking a creature with total concealment.

Second Step (Ex)

At 4th level, the knight of the round gains Improved Feint as a bonus feat, without needing to meet its prerequisites. If he already has the feat, he may take any combat feat which he qualifies for.

In addition, the knight of the round can make a feint as a swift action if they are dual wielding, and gains Bluff as a class skill.

Third Step (Ex)

At 7th level, the killer’s instinct in the knight of the round is honed to a razor’s fine edge, allowing them to add their Wisdom modifier as a competence bonus to confirm critical hits. This ability counts as if the character possessed the Critical Focus feat, and for the purposes of taking critical feats that the character qualifies for. The character may not select the Critical Focus feat once they have this ability, and should they have it before they gain this ability, they lose the Critical Focus feat and may select a critical feat in its place. You also gain a bonus critical feat that you meet the prerequisites for.

Fourth Step (Ex)

At 10th level, the knight of the round learns just how little they can trust their comrades. They cannot count towards having a teamwork feat, regardless of whether they have one. In return, they count themselves as an ally for them and are always under their effects. In addition, they gain a bonus teamwork feat of their choice that he meets the prerequisites for.

Fifth Step (Ex)

At 12th level, the knight of the round’s sneak attack can be applied to any opponent they threaten, that no other allies threaten, and only while no other enemies threaten them.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, the knight of the round can add their Wisdom modifier any time they deal sneak attack damage.

Seventh Step (Ex)

At 18th level, the knight of the round learns the art of targeting and avoiding armor. If they land more than one hit in a round that inflicts sneak attack damage, the target’s DR only applies once, not once per hit.

Palamedes

Knights of the round who follow Palamedes are master hunters and trackers, excelling in hunting down those who betray the order.

First Step (Ex)

The knight of the round that selects Palamedes hunts the foes of the order to the ends of the earth. By taking 1 minute to study a target, or their patterns through deeds and evidence, they can declare a specific target their quarry. They gain a +1 bonus on Charisma-based skills, Knowledge, and Sense Motive checks against the quarry, and a +1 bonus to weapon attack and damage rolls against it. In addition any knight of the round ability DCs are increased by 1 for the quarry. The knight of the round can only maintain one quarry at a time; these bonuses remain in effect until either the quarry is dead or the knight of the round selects a new quarry.

At 5th, 10th, 15th, the bonuses provided against the quarry and the DCs the quarry is subject to for knight of the round abilities, increase by 1.

At 7th level, the knight of the round can select a quarry by studying them or their patterns as a full-round action. Additionally, Survival is considered a class skill for the knight of the round and they gain a bonus on Survival checks to track their quarry equal to their class level.

Second Step (Ex)

Beginning at 4th level, as a swift action, when attacking your quarry with a weapon when they are flat-footed or denied their Dexterity bonus to AC, you may deal 1d6 additional damage per step ability you possess after the second. This is treated as sneak attack damage for any prerequisites or defenses on the part of the quarry.

Third Step (Ex)

Starting at 7th level, you may apply half the bonus you gain against your quarry to any allies of your quarry. This includes being able to apply half of your applicable sneak attack dice.

Fourth Step (Ex)

Beginning at 10th level, the knight of the round can perform a debilitating strike as a standard action against any creature for which he has a bonus from their 1st or 3rd step abilities.. If the attack hits, The target must make a Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 the knight of the round’s class level + their Dexterity modifier) or suffer one of the following conditions: blinded, nauseated, prone, or staggered. The condition lasts until the beginning of the knight of the round’s next turn. The knight of the round may still apply any feats or abilities to the single attack like Vital Strike.

Fifth Step (Ex)

Beginning at 12th level, when following the tracks of their quarry or their allies, they can take 10 on their Survival skill checks while moving at normal speed. Additionally, all critical hits against their quarry are automatically confirmed.

At 17th level, the knight of the round can instead take 20 on the Survival checks while moving at normal speed.

Sixth Step (Ex)

At 15th level, when using debilitating strike you can apply the stunned or dazed conditions. Additionally, you apply your bonuses against your quarry and their allies to CMB and CMD checks.

Seventh Step (Ex)

At 18th level, when making their debilitating attack from their fourth step ability, they can attempt to knock the target unconscious or kill them. However for these additional effects, the target does not have the DC increased by being a quarry or an ally thereof. Regardless of whether the target succeeded or failed their saving throw, they are immune to this improved debilitating strike for 24 hours.

Pellinore

Knights of the round who follow Pellinore master the forces of nature, protecting it and using it to strike those who aim to harm it.

First Step (Su)

At 1st level, the knight of the round gains a pool of natural points that fuel his other abilities. The number of points in this natural pool are equal to 1/2 of their class level + their Wisdom modifier, minimum 1. This recovers to full after an 8 hour rest.

Also at 1st level, the knight of the round can spend 1 point of his natural pool to grow protective thorns from their body for 1 minute per class level. These thorns deal magical piercing damage equal to 1d4 + their Wisdom modifier to anything that hits them with a melee attack. The number of d4 increases by 1 at the third, fifth and seventh steps.

Also at 1st level, the knight of the round may move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at her normal speed and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment. Thorns, briars, and overgrown areas that have been magically manipulated to impede motion, however, still affect her.

Second Step (Su)

At 4th level, the knight of the round can grant their first step feature to an ally, at the cost of 2 natural points.

Also at 4th level, the knight of the round can create items temporarily from greenwood, a rare wood only grow-able by those in tune with nature. Lasting 1 minute per class level, the knight of the round can, as a standard action and costing 1 natural point, create one item out of greenwood, such as a quarterstaff, longbow or something else primarily made of wood. The item is considered masterwork. The knight of the round can only have one greenwood item active at any time.

Ammo is generated for free as the weapon is fired Also at 4th level, the knight of the round can spend 1 natural point to gain the effects of speak with plants for 1 minute per level, with a caster level equal to their HD.

Third Step (Su)

At 7th level, the knight of the round’s second step ability creates weapons and armor of +1 enchantment quality, and the ammo for ranged weapons has the same bonus.

In addition, the knight of the round’s first step ability now deals 2d4 + their Wisdom modifier damage.

Fourth Step (Su)

At 10th level, at a cost of 2 natural points per day, the knight of the round can have one permanent greenwood item in their possession, and still create a second using their second step ability. In addition, all their created greenwood weapons and armor are now +2 enchantment quality and the ammo for ranged weapons has the same bonus. The permanent item can be enchanted as a normal weapon or armor, and maintains those enchantments for as long as the 2 points per day are spent.

Fifth Step (Su)

At 12th level, the knight of the round’s first step feature now deals 3d4 + their Wisdom modifier.

In addition, the knight of the round’s second step feature now creates weapons and armor of +3 enchantment quality, and the ammo for ranged weapons has the same bonus.

Sixth Step (Su)

At 15th level, the knight of the round can create a second permanent greenwood item, and all greenwood items are created at +4 enchantment quality.

Seventh Step (Su)

At 18th level, the knight of the round no longer has to pay points for their two permanent items, and can create up to their Wisdom modifier in items simultaneously, and maintain the same number.

In addition, their first step feature now deals 4d4 + their Wisdom modifier and the duration is doubled.

Tristan

Knights of the round who follow Tristan are masters of both blade and song, using both in a blended form to create beautiful battle.

First Step (Su)

The knight of the round that selects Tristan can sing a song of battle, empowering their allies to great deeds of valor. They gain the ability to inspire courage as a bard of their class level.

Additionally they gain bardic performance rounds as a bard of their class level, including for qualifying for feats, and the action required to initiate the performance.

Second Step (Su)

The road to battle can be long and hard, but a fine song can ease the passage of time.

Beginning at 4th level, they gain the ability to use song of marching from the skald class in addition to their inspire courage.

Third Step (Su)

The songs of battle can instill fear in the knight’s foes.

At 7th level, the knight of the round gains the ability to use the dirge of doom bardic performance.

Fourth Step (Su)

Songs can inspire anyone to great heights of bravery and worthiness of epic song.

At 10th level, the knight of the round may use the inspire greatness bardic performance using their class level as their effective bard level.

Fifth Step (Su)

The epic deeds recounted in song can drive the knight’s enemies before them.

At 12th level, they gain the ability to use the frightening tune bardic performance.

Sixth Step (Su)

Their ability to inspire bravery in their allies knows no bounds. The knight of the round gains the inspire heroics bardic performance.

Seventh Step (Su)

The knight can use their song to cause their allies to continue to fight even when times are dark and defeat seems imminent.

At 18th level, the knight of the round gains the ability to use the song of the fallen skald performance.
